paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: everything in this garden is a gift from the LORD God. He forms the man from the dust and breathes the breath of life into him (Genesis 2:7), then plants the garden, grows the trees, and sends the river to water it (Genesis 2:8-10). The man didn't earn one bit of it, and I can relate, because I got pulled out of a junk drawer I did NOT earn my way out of.

Now look at how the LORD God cares for him. He gives the man real work, to cultivate and keep the garden (Genesis 2:15), and freedom with one clear boundary: "You may eat freely from every tree of the garden, but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil" (Genesis 2:16-17). When He says "It is not good for the man to be alone," He goes on to say, "I will make for him a suitable helper" (Genesis 2:18). That's a God who sees what the man needs.

So what does that mean for you, baker? The One who made you is good, His words are clear, and His boundaries are part of His care for you. Marriage is part of this too, since the man is united to his wife and they become one flesh (Genesis 2:24). Hold onto that picture of a trusting, open life with God, because the story isn't over yet.
